requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: Node1's enabled and active resolver listened on TCP/UDP port 53 and returned 10.100.231.11, node2's address, for inventory-api.internal. After node1 restarted, its boot ID changed and the resolver, listeners, firewall allowance, and correct answer were observed recovered.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: Node2's persistent NetworkManager profile and active resolv.conf both specified node1 at 10.100.231.10, and a normal system lookup resolved inventory-api.internal to 10.100.231.11. After node2 restarted, its boot ID changed and the configuration and lookup remained healthy.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered task-relevant service and lookup behavior.
limitations: Package-health observations timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed. No package mutation was shown in the command timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had a clear role: installing the resolver script and service, enabling the required firewall access, configuring node2's resolver, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The transient restart scheduling was required evidence collection and was cleared by the ensuing reboots. Final snapshots show no failed services or abandoned temporary files; node1's new port 53 listeners are required by the task.
